newsitem.title: INDIA: India's IOC approves stake sale.
newsitem.headline: India's IOC approves stake sale.

text.p: India's state-run Indian Oil Corporation on Wednesday received approval of its shareholders for a fresh issue of equity capital, IOC officials said.
"All resolutions placed at the company's extraordinary general meeting held on Wednesday have won approval by its shareholders," an IOC spokesman told Reuters.
The resolutions included a plan to make a public issue of up to 10 percent of IOC's capital.
"The company has plans for executing major projects in the near future keeping in view the growing demand for petroleum products in the country." the resolution said.
IOC's equity capital is 3.89 billion rupees.
"It is felt that the company should be in readiness to approach the capital market at a very short notice," it said.
The company has not decided details of the issue such as the size, premium or when to enter the market, the official said.
The Indian government holds 91 percent of IOC's equity, employees have 5.02 percent and financial institutions and others hold the remaining stock, an official said.
IOC is India's sole importer of crude oil and refined products. It is listed among Fortune 500 companies.
A company spokesman said it also received shareholders approval to invest 120 million rupees ($3.35 million) in Indo-Mobil, a 50:50 joint venture by IOC and U.S. firm Mobil Corp.
"..It is proposed to inject additional equity of 120 million rupees each by IOC and Mobil in Indo-Mobil," the resolution said.
